title: Reunion
content:
The excitement of meeting Siddu again filled Sneha's heart throughout the week.

Every passing day felt unusually long, and with each sunrise, the weekend seemed to draw a little closer.

Miles away, Siddu, too, remembered the promise he had made to Sneha. As Friday came to an end, he packed his belongings and prepared for his journey to Shimla.

Saturday finally arrived.

Both of them set out from different cities, traveling toward the same destination, completely unaware that fate was once again bringing their paths together.

As the bus carried her through the winding mountain roads, Sneha rested her head against the window.

Outside, endless rows of pine trees stretched across the hills. White clouds drifted lazily between the mountains while the cool breeze slipped through the slightly open window, gently brushing against her face.

Yet her mind wasn't on the scenery.

Her thoughts drifted back to Rohini's words.

"I think you've started liking Siddharth."

A faint smile appeared on her lips.

"Why did she say that?" she whispered to herself.

One by one, memories from the train journey flashed before her eyes—Siddu's gentle smile, the concern hidden in his eyes, the way he spoke about his past, the note he had left behind, and the mysterious goodbye that had left her with countless unanswered questions.

Without realizing it, those memories had become precious to her.

Her heartbeat grew a little faster.

Do I... really love him?

The question lingered in her mind.

She wasn't ready to answer it.

With a shy smile, she gently shook her head and looked out at the breathtaking mountains, deciding to bury those feelings deep inside her heart—for now.

Meanwhile, Siddu's journey was equally silent.

Sitting by the window, he watched the mountains pass one after another.

A smile appeared on his face as he remembered the cheerful girl who had refused to let him keep his story unfinished.

"I wonder how many questions she's prepared for today," he murmured with a quiet laugh.

For the first time in many months, he felt strangely light.

The burden he had carried for so long seemed a little easier to bear.

Hours later, both of them finally arrived in Shimla.

The cool mountain breeze welcomed them as people hurried through the lively streets. Tourists wandered through the markets, children laughed while playing in the open square, and the aroma of freshly brewed coffee filled the crisp morning air.

Sneha looked around, searching through the crowd.

Then...

She saw him.

Siddu was standing a short distance away, wearing the same calm smile she remembered from the train.

For a few moments, the noise of the city faded into silence.

Neither of them moved.

Neither of them spoke.

They simply looked at each other after what felt like an eternity.

A gentle smile slowly appeared on Siddu's face as he walked toward her.

Stopping in front of Sneha, he looked into her eyes and quietly said,

"I'm sorry."

Sneha smiled softly and shook her head.

"You don't have to apologize," she replied. "I know whatever made you leave that day must have been important."

Relief washed over Siddu's face.

"Thank you... for understanding."

For a brief moment, neither of them knew what to say.

Then Sneha laughed softly.

"You know... I searched almost half the train looking for you."

Siddu looked at her in surprise.

"You did?"

"I even searched the neighboring coaches," she replied with a playful smile. "I thought maybe you'd gotten into the wrong compartment."

Siddu lowered his head with a guilty smile.

"I didn't know someone I'd met only a few hours earlier would go through so much trouble because of me."

Sneha folded her arms and looked away.

"Well... someone left his story unfinished."

Both of them laughed, and the remaining awkwardness between them disappeared.

They slowly began walking through the beautiful streets of Shimla.

As they walked, they admired the old colonial buildings, the bustling local shops, and the breathtaking view of the mountains stretching endlessly into the distance.

They spoke about their work, their college life, and the small events that had happened during the past week.

The conversation flowed effortlessly, as though they had known each other for years instead of only a few days.

After a leisurely walk, they entered a cozy café overlooking the hills.

The soft music playing in the background blended perfectly with the peaceful atmosphere.

They chose a table beside the large glass window, where they could watch the clouds slowly drift across the mountains.

A waiter arrived and took their order.

While waiting for the coffee, Sneha couldn't hold back any longer.

"So..." she asked with an excited smile, "are you going to make me wait again?"

Siddu chuckled.

"No."

A few moments later, two steaming cups of coffee were placed before them.

For a moment, Siddu stared quietly at the swirling steam rising from his cup.

He wrapped both hands around it and took a slow sip.

Then he lifted his eyes toward Sneha.

"I promised you something," he said.

Sneha smiled and nodded.

"You did."

Siddu took a deep breath.

"Then... let me continue the story from where I left it."
